--- title: Query with DuckDB description: Query the public OmicIDX Parquet with DuckDB over anonymous HTTPS. Covers the published database, the SRAdb- and GEOmetadb-compatible tables, and the raw source tables. --- OmicIDX publishes every table as Parquet over anonymous HTTPS. [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org) reads only the parts of each file that a query needs, so you can query tens of millions of rows from a laptop without downloading anything first. The examples on this page ran against `latest/` when the page was built. Each SQL example has an **Open in DuckDB Shell** link that runs it in your browser, and the [playground](../playground.qmd) has an editable query box. ## What's published The base URL is: ``` https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/ ``` (The older `https://data.omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/` serves the same files.) Under it, `latest/` is rebuilt every day (see [Schedule](../overview/data-sources.qmd#schedule)). Each day also gets an immutable `v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` folder: the 7 newest are kept, plus each week's last build (normally Sunday's) for 5 weeks. See [Versions and citation](versions-and-citation.qmd) for which to use, and [Releases](../releases.qmd) for what's there now. Each folder contains: | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `.parquet` | One file per source table: `sra_studies`, `sra_samples`, `sra_experiments`, `sra_runs`, `sra_accessions`, `geo_series`, `geo_samples`, `geo_platforms`, `geo_series_with_rnaseq_counts`, `biosamples`, `ebi_biosamples`, `bioprojects` | | `sradb/
.parquet` | SRAdb-compatible tables | | `geometadb/
.parquet` | GEOmetadb-compatible tables | | `omicidx.duckdb` | A small DuckDB database with a view over every Parquet file | | `views.sql` | The same views as plain SQL | | `restore.sql` | Builds a local copy of every table (see [Work offline](#work-offline)). Older dated folders don't have it | | `manifest.json` | Publish date, transform commit, lake snapshot id, row counts | You can browse a folder listing in your browser, e.g. [`latest/`](https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/). ## Attach the database `omicidx.duckdb` is a few hundred KB of view definitions. Attach it over HTTPS and query the views. The data stays remote. ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} ATTACH 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/omicidx.duckdb' AS omicidx (READ_ONLY); USE omicidx; ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT run_accession, study_title FROM sradb.rnaseq_runs WHERE taxon_id = 9606 -- human LIMIT 10; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |run_accession |study_title | |:-------------|:--------------------------------------------------------| |DRR415303 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415304 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415305 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415306 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415307 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415308 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415309 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415310 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415311 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines | |DRR415312 |RNA sequencing of Epstein-Barr virus-infected cell lines |
::: DuckDB loads its `httpfs` extension automatically for `https://` paths. If your install can't auto-load extensions, run `INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;` first. ## Read a Parquet file directly Every table is a plain file, so you can skip the database and use `read_parquet`: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT count(*) AS n FROM read_parquet('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/biosamples.parquet'); ```
Table: 1 records | n| |--------:| | 60758698|
::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT study_accession, title, study_type FROM 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sra_studies.parquet' WHERE bioproject = 'PRJNA1147303'; ```
Table: 1 records |study_accession |title |study_type | |:---------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------| |SRP525855 |Platelets Transfer Aldolase via Extracellular Vesicles to Facilitate the Metabolic Reprogramming of Kupffer Cells in Acute Liver Injury |Transcriptome Analysis |
::: Filters and column selection are pushed down, so only the matching parts of a file are fetched. ## SRAdb-compatible tables (`sradb`) A modernized [SRAdb](https://bioconductor.org/packages/SRAdb/) schema. Legacy column names are kept where the data still exists, always-empty columns are dropped, and BioProject, GEO, and PubMed cross-references are added. | Table | One row per | |---|---| | `sradb.study` | SRA study (SRP/ERP/DRP) | | `sradb.sample` | SRA sample (SRS/ERS/DRS) | | `sradb.experiment` | SRA experiment (SRX/ERX/DRX) | | `sradb.run` | SRA run (SRR/ERR/DRR) | | `sradb.sra` | run, joined with its experiment, sample, and study | | `sradb.run_with_study` | run, with study title, type, and BioProject | | `sradb.rnaseq_runs`, `sradb.wgs_runs` | `run_with_study` filtered by library strategy | | `sradb.human_runs`, `sradb.mouse_runs` | `run_with_study` filtered by taxon | ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT study_accession, study_title, bioproject_accession, pubmed_ids FROM sradb.study WHERE study_accession = 'SRP000001'; ```
Table: 1 records |study_accession |study_title |bioproject_accession |pubmed_ids | |:---------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------|:----------| |SRP000001 |Paired-end mapping reveals extensive structural variation in the human genome |PRJNA33627 |17901297 |
::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- RNA-seq runs for one BioProject SELECT run_accession, platform, instrument_model, total_bases FROM sradb.run_with_study WHERE bioproject = 'PRJNA1147303' AND library_strategy = 'RNA-Seq'; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |run_accession |platform |instrument_model | total_bases| |:-------------|:--------|:---------------------|-----------:| |SRR41116924 |DNBSEQ |DNBSEQ-T7 | 6633217200| |SRR41116925 |DNBSEQ |DNBSEQ-T7 | 6633141600| |SRR30213718 |ILLUMINA |Illumina NovaSeq 6000 | 6078034200| |SRR30213719 |ILLUMINA |Illumina NovaSeq 6000 | 7097461460| |SRR30213720 |ILLUMINA |Illumina NovaSeq 6000 | 5913186964| |SRR30213721 |ILLUMINA |Illumina NovaSeq 6000 | 5453278002| |SRR30213722 |DNBSEQ |DNBSEQ-T7 | 1194440800| |SRR30213723 |DNBSEQ |DNBSEQ-T7 | 1190760850| |SRR30213724 |DNBSEQ |DNBSEQ-T7 | 1194007300| |SRR30213725 |DNBSEQ |DNBSEQ-T7 | 1194538850|
::: ## GEOmetadb-compatible tables (`geometadb`) A modernized [GEOmetadb](https://bioconductor.org/packages/GEOmetadb/) schema: series (`gse`), samples (`gsm`), platforms (`gpl`), the `gse_gsm` and `gse_gpl` link tables, and `geo_supplemental_files`. ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- Series with NCBI-computed RNA-seq counts SELECT gse, title FROM geometadb.gse WHERE has_geo_computed_rnaseq LIMIT 10; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |gse |title | |:---------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |GSE124397 |SRSF1 role in cellular gene expression and splicing | |GSE97469 |Expression analysis of genes modulated after knock-down of lncRNA CHROME. | |GSE220530 |Human T cell characterisation | |GSE228549 |Endogenous expression of inactive lysine deacetylases KDAC6 (HDAC6) and KDAC8 (HDAC8) | |GSE108038 |Interleukin-4 restores neurogenic plasticity of the primary human neural stem cells through suppression of Kynurenic acid production upon Amyloid-beta42 toxicity | |GSE115310 |Abnormal RNA stability in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis | |GSE133495 |Transcriptomic profile of Calu-3 airway epithelial cells in response to flagellin | |GSE64927 |Effects of physiological and synthetic IAP antagonism on c-IAP dependent signaling | |GSE87581 |RNA-seq in endometrial stromal tumors | |GSE132194 |Global altered gene expression in triple-negative breast cancer tumor samples treated with CDK2 and EZH2 inhibitors |
::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- All samples in a series SELECT gsm FROM geometadb.gse_gsm WHERE gse = 'GSE118849'; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |gsm | |:----------| |GSM3349109 | |GSM3349110 | |GSM3349111 | |GSM3349112 | |GSM3349113 | |GSM3349114 | |GSM3349115 | |GSM3349116 | |GSM3349117 | |GSM3349118 |
::: ## Source tables The source tables (`sra_runs`, `geo_samples`, `biosamples`, …) keep the upstream record shape, including nested lists of attributes and identifiers. In `omicidx.duckdb` they're views in the default schema, so after `USE omicidx` you can write `FROM sra_studies`. Older dated databases contain only the `sradb` and `geometadb` views; use `read_parquet` for source tables there. ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} -- Unnest SRA study attributes SELECT accession, a.tag, a.value FROM 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sra_studies.parquet', unnest(attributes) AS t(a) LIMIT 10; ```
Table: Displaying records 1 - 10 |accession |tag |value | |:---------|:-----------------|:-----------| |SRP100657 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA351844 | |SRP100805 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA377164 | |SRP100828 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA378481 | |SRP100994 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA296358 | |SRP101007 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA296358 | |SRP101026 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA296358 | |SRP101027 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA296358 | |SRP101039 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA296358 | |SRP101051 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA296358 | |SRP101052 |parent_bioproject |PRJNA296358 |
::: ## Work offline For heavy use, make a local copy. `restore.sql` copies every table of a folder into a local DuckDB file, with the same schemas and names as the views, then checks each table's row count against the folder's `manifest.json`: ```bash curl -O https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/restore.sql duckdb omicidx-local.duckdb < restore.sql duckdb -readonly omicidx-local.duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM sradb.study" ``` A full copy is tens of GB, most of it `biosamples`. In R, [`omicidx_download()`](r-omicidxr.qmd#a-local-copy) does the same. To copy only a few tables, download their Parquet files and point DuckDB at them: ```bash curl -O https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sradb/study.parquet duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM 'study.parquet'" ``` ## Notes - Requests are anonymous HTTPS range requests. Behind a strict firewall, allow `omicidx.cancerdatasci.org`. - Any recent DuckDB release works. This page was built with DuckDB 1.5.6 (R package).
